facts.raw_span: persistent severe pain on the left side of her face
episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain initially affecting the entire left hemiface
pain localized to the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve
attacks lasted 4–5 seconds
triggered by jaw movement during eating or tooth brushing
reached 10/10 on a numeric pain scale
allodynia to cold air
hypersensitivity to touch in the affected area
distorted sensations in the V2 region
sensory testing was otherwise normal
no other neurological deficits
Contrast-enhanced MRI of the head showed no abnormalities

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are consistent with Trigeminal Neuralgia.
The patient developed symptoms of Trigeminal Neuralgia after receiving the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, suggesting a possible link between the vaccine and the condition.
The patient's symptoms of allodynia to cold air, hypersensitivity to touch, and distorted sensations in the V2 region are consistent with Atypical Trigeminal Neuralgia.

The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are consistent with Idiopathic Trigeminal Neuralgia.

The patient's symptoms of episodic sharp, electric-shock–like pain in the V2 and V3 distributions of the left trigeminal nerve, triggered by jaw movement, are consistent with Symptomatic Trigeminal Neuralgia.
The patient's symptoms of allodynia to cold air, hypersensitivity to touch, and distorted sensations in the V2 region are consistent with Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain.
The patient's symptoms of persistent severe pain on the left side of her face are consistent with Facial Pain Syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of allodynia to cold air, hypersensitivity to touch, and distorted sensations in the V2 region are consistent with Neuropathic Pain Syndrome.
The patient's symptoms of persistent severe pain on the left side of her face are consistent with Chronic Pain Syndrome.
The patient developed symptoms of neuropathic pain after receiving the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine, suggesting a possible link between the vaccine and the condition.
